title: Oscillations
summary: Simple harmonic motion arises from a restoring force proportional to displacement ($F=-kx$). Its motion is sinusoidal with period $T=2\pi\sqrt{m/k}$ (spring) or $2\pi\sqrt{L/g}$ (pendulum). Energy trades between kinetic and elastic potential.

simple harmonic motion.plain: Oscillation with a linear restoring force.

restoring force.plain: A force pulling back toward equilibrium.

SHM energy.plain: Trades between kinetic and elastic PE.

concept_sections.heading: The restoring force
concept_sections.explanation: SHM occurs when the restoring force is proportional to displacement: $F=-kx$. The minus sign means it always points back toward equilibrium.

concept_sections.heading: Period and frequency
concept_sections.explanation: For a mass–spring, $T=2\pi\sqrt{m/k}$; for a small-angle pendulum, $T=2\pi\sqrt{L/g}$. Frequency is $f=1/T$.

concept_sections.heading: The motion in time
concept_sections.explanation: Displacement follows $x(t)=A\cos(\omega t+\phi)$ with $\omega=\sqrt{k/m}$. Velocity and acceleration are its derivatives, peaking a quarter cycle apart.
math_steps: Max speed at equilibrium, max $|a|$ at the ends.

concept_sections.heading: Energy in SHM
concept_sections.explanation: Total energy $\tfrac12kA^2$ trades between kinetic and elastic potential. At the extremes it's all potential; at equilibrium all kinetic.
math_steps: At $x=A$: all PE; at $x=0$: all KE.

concept_sections.heading: The pendulum
concept_sections.explanation: A pendulum approximates SHM for small angles, with period depending only on length and gravity — not on mass or amplitude.

real_world_examples.title: A grandfather clock
real_world_examples.how_the_math_applies: Its period $2\pi\sqrt{L/g}$ depends only on length, so the clock is set by adjusting $L$.

real_world_examples.title: Car suspension
real_world_examples.how_the_math_applies: The suspension is a mass–spring oscillator; damping stops it from bouncing forever.

real_world_examples.title: A vibrating guitar string
real_world_examples.how_the_math_applies: It undergoes harmonic motion whose frequency sets the pitch.
